provenance.source: CTET Jul-2019 Paper-I. Poem text: Alfred Lord Tennyson, 'The Charge of the Light Brigade' (1854), as printed by the Poetry Foundation and poets.org.
provenance.method: the poem is identified from the questions themselves: Q100 asks for the figure of speech in 'the Valley of Death' and Q101 for the device in 'to do and die', both lines of Tennyson's poem, and Q102 asks what the soldiers are doing in the first stanza. Text taken from the published poem, not from a solved-paper rendering.
provenance.caveat: text is only added for the stimuli listed below; every other 2019 stimulus is still the importer's placeholder. No answer key has been applied for this cycle.
provenance.cycleNote: This cycle is the CTET December-2019 Paper-I, not July-2019: the Language-II English passage at Q129-135 ('Water is the core of life ... the bounty of the Himalayas', with the Uttarakhand perennial-streams paragraph) is the December-2019 one, and Testbook tags these questions 'CTET December 2019 Paper 1'.
provenance.officialKey: The official final answer key for this paper is https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s3443dec3062d0286986e21dc0631734c9/uploads/2022/03/2022033144.pdf (linked from https://ctet.nic.in/document/ctet-december-2019-paper-1/). It has not been read yet, so no answer has been changed for this cycle. It is needed before the Q129-135 answers are trusted: theexampillar numbers the block 129 part-of-speech, 130 'central to our thinking', 131 'not been mentioned', 133 Uttarakhand, 134 'bounty', 135 'benevolent', while studyfry numbers the same questions 134, 135, 129, 131, 132, 133 - the two disagree, and the bank follows theexampillar's order. Only the official key can settle both the order and the answers.

stimuli.text:
Half a league, half a league,
Half a league onward,
All in the valley of Death
Rode the six hundred.
"Forward, the Light Brigade!
Charge for the guns!" he said.
Into the valley of Death
Rode the six hundred.

"Forward, the Light Brigade!"
Was there a man dismayed?
Not though the soldier knew
Someone had blundered.
Theirs not to make reply,
Theirs not to reason why,
Theirs but to do and die.
Into the valley of Death
Rode the six hundred.
stimuli.note: The placeholder held Blake's 'Evening Star' - a real poem, but the wrong one: Q100 and Q101 quote 'the Valley of Death' and 'to do and die', which are Tennyson's. Stanzas I and II are given, which is the extract the questions run against (Q102 asks about the first stanza, Q104 about 'not to reason why' / 'to do and die'). Spelling follows the Poetry Foundation's modernised text ('dismayed', 'blundered', 'Theirs'). Line-leading indentation is dropped on purpose: the bank's text sanitizer collapses it, and if the source kept the three-space indent the apply tool would never see the block as current and would rewrite the file on every run.
stimuli.instructions: Direction: Read the extract given below and answer the questions that follow (Q. No. 100 to 105) by selecting the correct/most appropriate options:

stimuli.text:
Water is the core of life; hence water must be central to our spiritual thinking. Water is not only most of earth, but also most of life. Therefore water conservation must be our deepest concern.

The Himalayas serve as water towers, providing water on a sustained basis to more than 1,000 million people and millions of hectares of land in South Asia. The greenery, benevolent climate, highly productive ecosystems, food production and overall happiness in South Asia are in fact, attributable to the bounty of the Himalayas. They are not only beautiful; they are life-givers. Little wonder that they are venerated as the abode of gods.

The Himalayas in the state of Uttarakhand are especially rich in water resources. This area is home to dozens of perennial streams and numerous other rain-fed rivers along with innumerable rivulets, waterfalls and ponds, etc.
stimuli.note: Assembled from four independent renderings of the same CTET December-2019 passage, which agree on the wording: theexampillar and studyfry give the first two paragraphs, vidhyarthidarpan gives the Uttarakhand paragraph, and Testbook supplies the sentence 'They are not only beautiful; they are life-givers. Little wonder that they are venerated as the abode of gods.' between them. Every phrase the seven questions turn on is present - 'bounty', 'benevolent', 'perennial streams', the Uttarakhand list (streams, rain-fed rivers, rivulets, waterfalls, ponds) that Q133 needs, and 'core of life' for Q130. The answers for this block have NOT been changed: theexampillar and studyfry number these questions differently and only the official key can settle it.
stimuli.instructions: Direction: Read the passage given below and answer the questions that follow (Q. Nos. 129 to 135) by selecting the correct/most appropriate options:
निर्देश : निम्नलिखित गद्यांश को पढ़कर पूछे गए प्रश्नों (प्रश्न सं. 129 से 135 तक) के सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर वाले विकल्प चुनिए:
stimuli.text:
आज जब भी कोई गाँव का नाम लेता है तो एक अलग ही छवि उभरती है। वह छवि कहती है कि वहाँ गरीबी है। वहाँ अशिक्षा और अज्ञान है। वहाँ अंध-विश्वास है। गंदगी है। बीमारी है। हमें विचार करना है कि सच क्या है? क्या हमारे गाँव ऐसे ही थे जैसे आज हैं? आज जो गाँवों की दुर्दशा हुई है उसके लिए जिम्मेदार कौन है? इन सवालों की पड़ताल करते हुए हमें नई समझ बनानी है तथा गाँवों के सही स्वरूप की पहचान करनी है। वैसे यह खुदा का शुक्र है कि गाँवों पर कई तरह के आक्रामक दुष्प्रभावों के बावजूद उनका मूल स्वरूप नहीं बदला है। जो दूरस्थ गाँव हैं – शहर के पड़ोस से दूर उनकी निजता तो खासी बची हुई है। ऐसी स्थिति में हमारा दायित्व, एक शिक्षित समाज का दायित्व क्या बनाता है? हमें विचार करना है। मगर ऐसा कोई भी विचार गाँवों को आँखों से देखे बिना, स्वयं देख कर समझे बिना नहीं किया जा सकता। तो हमें अपनी फर्स्ट हैंड समझ बनाने के लिए गाँव चलना है।

अपने मूल स्वरूप में गाँव एक वेधशाला है। एक विद्याशाला है। गाँव वेधशाला या प्रयोगशाला इसलिए है कि ज्ञान को रोज वहाँ कर्म की कसौटी पर कसा जाता है। आजमाया जाता है। जो ज्ञान कर्म की कसौटी पर खरा न उतरे तो उसे खारिज कर दिया जाता है। हर ज्ञान के होने की शर्त यह है वह सृजन और उत्पादन की शान पर तराशा जाए।
stimuli.note: Replaces an invented placeholder about मातृभाषा that had nothing to do with the questions, which are all about गाँव as वेधशाला/प्रयोगशाला. Source: Testbook's rendering of CTET December 2019 Paper 1 (Hindi) at testbook.com/question-answer/ques--5eecc910dafe960d1664c872, which carries Q131 against this passage. All seven bank answers for Q129-135 were checked against this text and follow from it: Q129 सृजन और उत्पादन, Q132 कर्म की कसौटी, Q131 स्वयं गाँव में जाना, and Q135 asks what is NOT in the village's image - the passage lists गरीबी, अशिक्षा, अज्ञान, अंध-विश्वास, गंदगी and बीमारी, so कर्म is the odd one out. Caveat: a studyfry page for '2019' carries a different 129-135 passage (about नश्वर शरीर); that is another set or sitting, not this one.

stimuli.instructions: Direction: Read the passage given below and answer the questions that follow (Q. Nos. 121 to 128) by selecting the correct/most appropriate options:
stimuli.text:
Freedom is one of the most important factors in life. Man has fought politically all over the world for freedom. Religions have promised freedom, not in this world but in another. In the capitalist countries, individual freedom exists to some degree, and in the communist world it has been denied. From ancient times, freedom has meant a great deal to man, and there have been its opponents, not only political but religious through Inquisition, by excommunication, tortures and banishments, and the total denial of man’s search for freedom. There have been wars and counter-wars fought for freedom. This has been the pattern of man’s endeavours for freedom throughout history.

Freedom of self-expression and freedom of speech and thought exist in some parts of the world, but in others it does not. Those who have been conditioned, revolt against their backgrounds. This reaction which takes different forms is called ‘freedom’. The reaction to politics is often to shun the field of politics.

One economic reaction is to form small communities based on some ideology or under the leadership of one person, but these soon disintegrate. The religious reaction against established organisations of belief is to revolt, either by joining other religious organisations or by following some guru or leader or by joining some cult. Or one denies the whole religious endeavour.

One thinks of freedom only as freedom of movement, either physical or movements of thought. It appears that one always seeks freedom on the surface. Surely, this is rather a limited freedom, involving a great deal of conflict, wars and violence.

Inner freedom is something entirely different. It has its roots not in the idea of freedom but in the reality of freedom. It covers all the endeavours of man. Without inner freedom life will always be an activity within the limited circle of time and conflict.
stimuli.note: Replaces an invented placeholder about cultural exchange between civilizations, which had nothing to do with the questions. Source: Testbook's Comprehension block for CTET December 2019 Paper 1 at testbook.com/question-answer/which-methods-do-authorities-not-use-to-suppress-p--5eeca619dafe960d13e718ff, cross-checked against studyfry and vidhyarthidarpan renderings of the same paper. All eight bank answers follow from this text: 'endeavours' = attempts and 'shun' (the passage's 'shun the field of politics') = the opposite is welcome; the methods listed are Inquisition, excommunication, tortures and banishments, so Persuasion is the one not used; 'Freedom is one of the most important factors in life' makes 'Freedom is not one of the most important factors' the untrue statement; the religious revolt is by joining other organisations, following a guru or joining a cult, not by starting a new religion; real freedom is the passage's inner freedom; and for the A/B pair, A is false because the passage says individual freedom exists to some degree in capitalist countries, while B is true because it says it has been denied in the communist world. Q123 is a sentence-correction item that does not need the passage. Note that the bank's question ids for this cycle carry the set token 'a' while the paper this text comes from is published as Set D; the question texts match, and the set token in a bank id is not the CBSE set letter.
